title: Security answers delivery latency tiering and crediting strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define a delivery and crediting model for Security Questionnaires (SIG/CAIQ and large custom questionnaires) that balances customer SLAs, internal engineering effort, and monetization. The proposal introduces latency tiers for answer delivery, an attachable credit currency for paid expedited responses, and an automated issuance path for repeatable responses.

Background: Large enterprise RFPs and procurement cycles frequently request completed SIG/CAIQs and bespoke security questionnaires. Our sales and solutions teams spend ~40% of manual effort per large account on composing curated answers, and legal/security teams spend additional cycles validating claims. Existing self-serve attestation packs are either free but manual or packaged as large paid bundles that are inflexible.

Goals:
- Reduce average time-to-first-complete-response for high-priority accounts while containing support headcount growth.
- Introduce a consumption mechanism (credits) tied to explicit delivery tiers to recover marginal cost of human/engineering effort for expedited deliveries.
- Maintain a self-serve pathway for low-effort customers and an automated issuance flow for high-frequency, low-variance answers.
- Preserve compliance; every paid/auto-issued attestation must leave an audit trail and be verifiable (KMS-signed PDF or tokenized export).

Proposed model:
1) Latency tiers (customer-facing):
   - Instant (templated self-serve): immediate, free for included baseline answers; customers get a machine-generated SIG/CAIQ with best-effort citations from docs.
   - Standard (managed, 3 business days): default for enterprise customers; includes human review and packaging.
   - Expedited (prioritized, 48 hours): paid via credits; SLA-backed time-to-delivery.
   - Concierge (custom, variable): high-touch, quoted as professional services.

2) Crediting & pricing:
   - Credits per export: small fee per exported attestation bundle (covers formatting/export costs).
   - Credits per expedited batch: a larger credit cost applied when choosing Expedited tier.
   - Question-level crediting: optionally charge credits for custom question answers when complexity is high (manual research required).
   - Credit purchase & burn model exposed in Console and invoiced monthly for enterprise accounts.

3) Automation & reuse:
   - Answer canonicalization: store canonical answers per question with metadata (model version, last reviewed, owner).
   - Auto-issue rules: when canonical answer exists and last review <12 months old, allow Instant/Instant+KMS sign route.
   - Audit trail: every issued bundle stores source canonical IDs, review history, signer, and export hash.

Experiment plan:
- Pilot cohort: 10 existing enterprise accounts undergoing active procurement; split into A (current process) and B (tiered model with credits).
- Duration: 8 weeks.
- Metrics: time-to-first-complete-response, manual engineer hours per ticket, revenue from credits, number of auto-issued bundles, customer satisfaction (NPS small survey), number of downstream legal exceptions.
- Success criteria: 30% reduction in manual hours per attestation, positive net revenue from credits at pilot scale, no increase in security exceptions.

Stakeholders: Product (Maya Chen, Aaron Li), Solutions & Sales (Priya Kumar), Legal & Security (Daniel Rhodes), Eng (runtime and export team), DX (Docs & Console), Finance (pricing validation).

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix and credit SKU design.
- Console UX flows for purchasing credits and selecting latency tiers.
- Backend: export generator, KMS-signed export pipeline, billing hooks.
- Canonical answer datastore schema and review UI.
- Pilot onboarding checklist and playbook for SEs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers view credits as nickel-and-diming. Mitigation: bundle a small free credit allowance for new enterprise tiers and provide a cost-offset for long-term contracts.
- Risk: increased workload for security reviewers. Mitigation: enforce auto-issue rules and require human review only for flagged answers or high-risk answers.
- Risk: compliance gaps in auto-issued answers. Mitigation: KMS signing and mandatory periodic reviews + audit logs.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the product design and pilot plan. Separate ENG tickets will be created for export plumbing, KMS integration, and billing connectors.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Pricing matrix documented with credit SKUs, cost-per-export and cost-per-expedite defined and approved by Finance
AC-2: Console mockups for credit purchase and latency tier selection reviewed by DX and approved by PM
AC-3: Pilot playbook including SE onboarding, templated responses, and escalation path published in Confluence
AC-4: Security sign-off on auto-issue rules and KMS signing approach (evidence captured in Confluence)
AC-5: Metrics dashboard defined with instrumentation requirements for pilot (time-to-response, credits consumed, manual hours)
notes: Design trade-off: question-level crediting increases billing accuracy but complicates UX—initial pilot will focus on bundle & expedite credits only
Canonicalization approach should reuse existing answers from the Answers Library (see PM-31211) wherever possible
We will default to Standard tier for all new enterprise attestation requests unless SE opts in to Expedited
Security review required for auto-issue flow and KMS export; track as gating item for pilot launch
